newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Attackers wound helper of China activists in HK.
newsitem.headline: Attackers wound helper of China activists in HK.

text.p: Unknown assailants have staged a bloody knife attack on a Hong Kong man who helped democracy activists flee China after Beijing's crackdown in 1989, a legislator said on Friday.

Chan Tat-ching, a trading firm proprietor, aged about 50, was in a critical condition following Thursday's attack, which occurred while he was eating out, Democratic Party legislator Lau Chin-shek told Reuters after visiting Chan in hospital.
"He couldn't talk and was unconscious," Lau said.

Beijing accused Chan in the early 1990s of helping activists leave China after the Tiananmen Square crackdown in Beijing, Lau said. Chan was an important figure in the escape route popularly known as Operation Yellowbird, Lau said.
A police spokeswoman confirmed to Reuters that a 50-year-old man named Chan had been hacked by three to four attackers while sitting at a food stall table with two other men on Thursday.
She declined to name the victim. The motive for the attack was not yet clear and nobody had yet been arrested as of Friday morning, she said.
